concepts.def: The chip that executes program instructions through the fetch-decode-execute cycle, containing the control unit, ALU and registers.
A very small, very fast storage location inside the CPU holding one value during processing, such as an address, instruction or result.
The sets of connections carrying information inside a computer: addresses on the address bus, data on the data bus, signals on the control bus.
A computer system with a dedicated function built into a larger device, such as the controller inside a washing machine or car engine.
Secondary storage with no moving parts that stores data in flash memory chips, making it fast, quiet and resistant to shocks.
Secondary storage such as CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray discs, read by shining a laser onto the disc's reflective surface.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hardware — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Hardware brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Hardware.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which storage technology has no moving parts?
options: Solid-state drive (SSD)
Magnetic hard disk drive
DVD drive
Cassette tape

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of an embedded system?
options: The microprocessor controlling a washing machine
A gaming desktop PC
A spreadsheet application
A computer mouse mat

mcqs.q: The data bus is used to:
options: Carry data between the processor, memory and other components
Hold the address of the next instruction
Cool the motherboard
Store files permanently

mcqs.q: Which of these is optical storage?
options: A Blu-ray disc
An SSD
A USB flash drive
RAM

mcqs.q: Is an SSD a type of RAM?
options: No - an SSD is non-volatile secondary storage that keeps files when the power is off; RAM is volatile main memory used while programs run.
Yes - storage is measured by weight.
Yes - installing an SSD increases the computer's RAM.
Yes - SSDs are just large RAM chips, so they do the same job.

mcqs.q: Does a physically bigger device always have more storage capacity?
options: Yes - larger boxes always contain more gigabytes.
Yes - embedded systems include a full app store.
No - capacity depends on the storage technology and density, not physical size; a tiny microSD card can hold more than a large old hard drive.
Yes - storage is measured by weight.

mcqs.q: Can you install your own choice of applications on an embedded system?
options: Yes - every device with a chip can run any app.
Yes - embedded systems include a full app store.
No - embedded systems run fixed, dedicated software for one function; unlike a general-purpose PC, they are not designed for user-installed programs.
Yes - storage is measured by weight.
